body:
T222 (landing) journals INTENT before `federate`: `syncChannel` appends the ids about to be
ingested as an optimistic debt, so a crash between the two writes heals. This ticket hardens the
soup shape that journal-before-federate opens. Do NOT relitigate T222; extend it.

THE DEFECT, verified real. Both pull sources re-offer their whole set every poll; neither is
cursor-based. `federate` REJECTS an invalid-signature delta and never pools it. So a peer that
keeps offering one invalid-signature delta W makes `declared` name W on every poll: W is never
pooled, so `pooled` never contains it, so `declared.length > owed.length` stays true, so the
journal fires every poll. That is two channel records per poll without bound (the journal plus the
success stamp), on top of the pre-existing one-per-poll success stamp this doubles.

WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not a completeness lie: W is never stamped, and the trail stays honest. It
needs invalid-signature deltas, which means corruption or malice, not normal operation. But it is
Myk's delta-soup shape, it is peer-driven, and it is the inherent cost of journalling before
`federate`.

THE FIX needs STATE or a REDESIGN. A bounded fix remembers a rejected id and does not re-journal
it. The alternative is to journal AFTER `federate` using `report.acceptedIds`: that removes this
soup, but it reopens a smaller crash window (a crash between `federate` landing and the journal
write). Weigh the two; T222 chose journal-first to close the wider window, so a redesign must not
silently reopen it.

Acceptance criteria:
(a) A standing sync against a peer that re-offers ONE invalid-signature delta every poll appends a
    BOUNDED count of channel records over K polls, not O(K). Verify: a new case in
    `test/federation/` that polls K times against such a peer and asserts the operator-authored
    channel-record count stays bounded as K grows.
(b) The trail stays honest and two-sided: the rejected delta is never stamped and is not carried as
    owed once dropped, WHILE a valid delta on the same channel still journals and stamps exactly
    once. Verify: same file, assert over pool arrival stamps (delta level) and `channelStatus`
    (object level).
(c) No T222 regression: a normal accepting sync still appends at most one journal record beyond the
    success stamp, and a quiet sync appends none. Verify: `test/federation/crash-window.test.ts`
    case (b) stays green.

Merge tier: hardening on the T222 mechanism. A state-carrying or redesign change to what the sync
writes is a decision — surface it for Myk rather than self-merging.
title: A persistently-rejected peer offer must not inflate the channel-record rate
